rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Unit 2 defines communication as the exchange of information, ideas, feelings and meaning between two or more people through symbols, signs or behaviour. It sets out the six elements - sender, message, channel, receiver, feedback and noise - and the types, including verbal, non-verbal, visual and active listening.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Communication is not only talking; it also includes listening, observing and interpreting.
Noise is any interference that distorts the message.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: ❌ Communication is only talking. ✅ It includes listening, observing, and interpreting.  ·  ❌ More words = better communication. ✅ Clarity and conciseness matter more.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Do not answer 'Communication means talking only' - the notes explicitly reject this.  ·  In a diagram, label all six elements and show noise interfering with the channel.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Explain the elements of communication with a diagram.  ·  What are the barriers to effective communication? How can they be overcome?

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Do not write that more words make communication better; clarity and conciseness are what matter.  ·  Keep the answers themselves clear and concise - the 5 Cs apply to your writing too.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Differentiate between verbal and non-verbal communication with examples.  ·  List the barriers to effective communication and explain how they can be overcome.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Mnemonic for the six elements: 'Some Messages Change Hands, Not Fully' - Sender, Message, Channel, Receiver, Feedback, Noise.  ·  Reject any option that defines communication as only speaking.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: Explain the elements of communication with a suitable diagram.  ·  Explain the 5 Cs of effective communication.

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Elements with a diagram, barriers and types are all common question types in this unit.  ·  MCQ traps: treating the medium as the person who sends the message, or treating noise as the feedback.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Communication as the exchange of information, ideas, feelings and meaning through symbols, signs or behaviour  ·  The six elements: sender, message, channel or medium, receiver, feedback and noise  ·  Types of communication: verbal, non-verbal, visual and active listening  ·  Four barriers: physical, psychological, semantic and cultural

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Six elements in order: sender, message, channel or medium, receiver, feedback and noise.  ·  The channel or medium is the method of transmission (verbal, written, digital), not the person who sends the message.  ·  Non-verbal communication covers body language, gestures and facial expressions.  ·  Four barriers: physical (distance, noise), psychological (prejudice, emotion), semantic (language differences), cultural (norms, values).

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: Distinguish between physical, psychological, semantic and cultural barriers with one example of each.  ·  Why is active listening important? Explain.

rows.label: More hints
rows.text: Open a long answer with a one-line definition of communication, then list the elements, then the barriers.  ·  This unit is content and vocabulary based; do not add grammar rules that are not in these notes.

rows.label: MCQ drill
rows.text: In the communication process, the person who gets the message is the: → C  ·  Which of the following is one of the six elements of communication? → A

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ### 1. What is Communication?  ·  Communication is the exchange of information, ideas, feelings, and meaning between two or more people through symbols, signs, or behavior.  ·  ### 2. Elements of Communication

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: The 5 Cs of effective communication: clarity, conciseness, correctness, courtesy and confidence  ·  Active listening as fully concentrating on what is being said  ·  The 5 Cs of effective communication are clarity, conciseness, correctness, courtesy and confidence.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Feedback is the receiver's response and is what completes the communication process.  ·  Active listening belongs with the types in these notes; it is not one of the six elements and not a barrier.  ·  Verbal communication uses spoken or written words, while non-verbal communication uses body language, gestures and facial expressions.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Visual communication uses images, graphs and symbols.  ·  More words do not make communication better; clarity and conciseness matter more.  ·  Physical barriers include distance and noise, and semantic barriers arise from differences in language.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Barrier keyword test: distance or noise = physical; prejudice or emotion = psychological; language difference = semantic; norms or values = cultural.  ·  For 5 Cs questions, write the five words in a single line first, then explain each - this prevents forgetting one.  ·  If a question asks which element completes the process, the answer is feedback.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Differentiate between verbal and non-verbal communication.  ·  Explain the 5 Cs of effective communication with a short example for each.  ·  Describe active listening and its importance in a face-to-face conversation.
